parent: Worldpay (Worldpay Holdco, LLC; majority owned by GTCR)
notes: JobsOhio's release says Worldpay reestablished its global corporate headquarters in Cincinnati (Symmes Township) on separating from FIS, with GTCR buying a majority stake at an $18.5 billion valuation. FIS's FY2023 10-K reports more than 60,000 employees at Dec. 31, 2023 and about 52,000 as of Feb. 1, 2024 after completing the Worldpay sale, so roughly 8,000 employees went with Worldpay; JobsOhio's 2024 report shows 971 Cincinnati jobs retained and 529 committed.

SEC filings for CIK 723258 show this EIN's registrant was renamed from Great American Life Insurance Company to MassMutual Ascend Life Insurance Company on Oct. 3, 2022 and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance Company (Springfield, MA) following AFG's May 2021 sale; the same filing shows Glidepath Holdings, Inc., the name under which JobsOhio booked the $1.5 million Economic Development Grant in September 2022, is the MassMutual subsidiary that supplies MassMutual Ascend's personnel. No worldwide employee count for MassMutual was found in any filing or on its website, so the 5000+ bucket rests on its scale as a Fortune 500 mutual insurer plus the 633 Cincinnati jobs JobsOhio recorded as retained.

Smucker Innovation, Inc. is the entity JobsOhio named for the $1 million Research and Development Grant for the new Orrville R&D center (Wayne County, 1,795 jobs retained). Smucker's FY2025 10-K reports over 8,000 full-time employees worldwide, headquarters in Orrville, Ohio, and that the company was established in 1897 and incorporated in Ohio in 1921.

parent: West Warren Development LLC (Charles 'Chuck' George and two other managing partners)
notes: Single-purpose vehicle for the West Warren Industrial Park, an 86-acre speculative park on the former Warren Western Reserve High School site; WKBN reported the first 100,000 square foot building was being built with no tenant committed, which is what the JobsOhio Spec Development Grant and Loan under OSIP paid for. Ohio Capital Journal, following a WFMJ investigation, reports the developer is West Warren Development LLC, formed March 17, 2022, one of whose three managing partners is Charles George, then president of the board of Lake to River Economic Development, a JobsOhio network partner, and a Team NEO board member. No employee count is published for the developer; <100 is the bucket a three-partner development firm supports.

parent: Top Property Holdings, LLC (owner Greg Toporcer)
notes: JobsOhio's own release names Greg Toporcer as owner of Top Property, a Mahoning Valley developer that builds class-A industrial space with no committed tenant; his earlier North Jackson spec building was leased to Shapes Unlimited. The grant and loan came through the Ohio Site Inventory Program, so the business here is real estate built for others. No employee count is published for the firm; <100 fits an owner-run developer.

Chicago hot dog and pickle maker, founded 1893, headquartered in Chicago; the $500,000 JobsOhio Revitalization Grant paid to clean up and fit out a Newcomerstown building that became its third pickle plant, with 51 jobs committed and $18.5 million invested. This is an operating food manufacturer spending on its own plant, not a developer. No published company-wide employee count was found; Wikipedia gives revenue of about $130 million, and the bucket is a judgment from that scale, so it could be 500-4999.

Agracel is an industrial developer headquartered in Effingham, Illinois; its president, Ryan Witges, is quoted in JobsOhio's release on the 50,000 square foot speculative building it is developing at Growing Acres Industrial Park in Mercer County under the Ohio Site Inventory Program. Developing and leasing buildings for other companies is Agracel's actual business, so site_development is the right class. No employee count is published; <100 fits a regional developer.

Curious Real Estate LLC is the property vehicle for Curiosity, a Cincinnati advertising agency; the $280,000 payment matches the JobsOhio Revitalization Grant booked in November 2023 to Curiosity, LLC in Hamilton County against a $3,318,512 investment, and the recipient's address, 1544 Central Parkway, is the larger Cincinnati building the agency's release says it needed. The money built the agency's own office, so this is a business, not a developer. JobsOhio's release says Curiosity was founded in Ohio in 2012 and is led by its ownership group.

JobsOhio's releases name Aaron Neff as owner of 4 Friends LLC, which spent about $1.5 million renovating the 1920 former Sipe Chevrolet building at 1023 Wheeling Avenue in Cambridge into the Midtown Market, a 17,260 square foot mixed-use market leased to six to eight food vendors, a bar, a business cooperative and co-working tenants. The grant came through the Vibrant Community Program, whose purpose is real estate and shared space, and the LLC's business is owning and leasing the building, so site_development fits. No employee count is published for the LLC; the project committed 39 jobs across its tenants.

parent: Hanwha Solutions Corporation (Qcells; part of Hanwha Group)
notes: JobsOhio's 2024 report shows a $200,000 Revitalization Grant to FLEXRACK by Qcells LLC in Mahoning County, advanced manufacturing, 27 jobs created and 23 retained against $10.1 million invested, for the solar racking maker's move into the former Things Remembered building; the money cleaned up and fitted out its own plant, so this is a business. Wikipedia shows Qcells' parent is Hanwha Solutions Corporation of Seoul, with 6,004 employees in 2023, itself part of Hanwha Group. No release confirming the FLEXRACK-Qcells ownership link was found beyond the entity's own name, so this is graded C.

JobsOhio's release says Ark Transportation, a freight and logistics firm, made 13000 Darice Parkway in Strongsville its global headquarters in 2024 and that the company 'has been in Northeast Ohio' from the beginning; no outside parent is named. JobsOhio's 2024 report shows 36 jobs retained in Cuyahoga County and 103 committed, so the company may have passed 100 employees by the cash year; the bucket uses the retained figure, which is the only count actually reported.

JobsOhio's 2023 report shows a $150,000 Economic Development Grant to RDP Foodservice, LTD in Franklin County, logistics and distribution, with 113 jobs retained and 40 committed against an $8 million investment, which puts it in the 100-499 bucket. Its own site describes it as a family food distributor serving central Ohio from Hilliard; no parent company was found.

The $125,000 matches JobsOhio's July 2024 Revitalization Grant of exactly $125,000 to Phoenix Steel Service, Inc. in Cuyahoga County, advanced manufacturing, 23 jobs created and 65 retained against $5.34 million invested, so Phoenix Steel Processing LLC is the payee vehicle for the Cleveland steel service centre's own plant project. Class is business for that reason; 88 jobs created plus retained keeps it under 100.

parent: Brush Run Holdings LLC (operating company not identified)
notes: Unresolved. The 990 gives only a PO box in Baltic, Ohio, which sits where Tuscarawas, Holmes and Coshocton counties meet. No row in JobsOhio's monthly executed-grants reports matches the name, and none of the $100,000 awards in those three counties in 2023 to 2025 (ProVia Payroll, Gerber and Sons, Holmes Siding Contractors) names Baltic. Google News has nothing, and the Ohio Secretary of State business search was offline for maintenance throughout this research, so the member behind the LLC could not be checked. Class and bucket are the best guess from the $100,000 size, which matches JobsOhio's Revitalization and Economic Development grants to small operating companies in that area; the class could be site_development if the LLC is purely a property vehicle.

JobsOhio's 2023 report shows a $100,000 Economic Development Grant to Mattr US Inc. across Butler and Hamilton counties, advanced manufacturing, 48 jobs created and 26 retained against $8.06 million invested, matching press coverage of a heat-shrink tubing plant expansion in Fairfield; the US entity is the Ohio arm of Mattr Corp. of Toronto, the former Shawcor. The only employee figure found anywhere is Wikipedia's 6,000 from November 2017 under the Shawcor name; Mattr has divested businesses since, so the grant-year figure may actually fall in 500-4999. Graded D for that reason.

JobsOhio's September 2024 report shows a $100,000 Revitalization Grant to The Safety Company, LLC in Cuyahoga County with 20 jobs created and 21 retained against $925,000 invested; the grant cleaned up and fitted out the company's own Garfield Heights site, so this is a business. 41 jobs created plus retained keeps it under 100, and no parent company was found.

JobsOhio's February 2024 report names GFFC Holdings, LLC itself as the company for a $75,000 Economic Development Grant in Fulton County, advanced manufacturing, 22 jobs created and none retained against $285,500 invested, so it is an operating manufacturer starting up in Wauseon rather than a real-estate vehicle. What the initials stand for could not be established: there is no news coverage, no company website found, and the Ohio Secretary of State business search was offline during this research, so the possibility of a parent above it is open. Graded C.

Hexpol Compounding LLC is the US rubber compounding arm of HEXPOL AB, the Malmo, Sweden polymer group spun out of Hexagon AB in 2008, which the Swedish Wikipedia entry records at 5,010 employees in December 2024. JobsOhio's 2021 report shows the $72,500 Revitalization Grant for its Summit County site, 7 jobs created and 19 retained against $2.48 million invested; the grant cleaned up HEXPOL's own plant. The employee figure comes from an encyclopedia entry rather than the group's own report, which Cloudflare blocked, so this is graded C and sits just over the 5,000 line.

JobsOhio's November 2023 report shows a $50,000 Inclusion Grant to A-1 Printing LLC in Crawford County, advanced manufacturing, 2 jobs created and 12 retained against $360,549 invested. The Inclusion Grant is restricted to small businesses and capped at $50,000, and 12 retained jobs confirms the size; no parent company was found.

JobsOhio's September 2023 report shows a $50,000 Inclusion Grant to B&H Butchery, LLC in Belmont County, food and agribusiness, 2 jobs created and 2 retained against $230,000 invested. The Inclusion Grant is capped at $50,000 and limited to small businesses; no parent company was found.
